name: Legal document

documentRef.note: An ENUM of the two real documents, not a body field. A PageSpec can only point at an existing signed-off document; it cannot carry legal prose.

sectionCount.note: terms-of-use has 25 top-level sections, privacy-policy has 12. Recorded for structural validation only.

constraints.noHero: This template has no hero. The document title is the top of the page.
constraints.noTableOfContents: No TOC, no jump-link list, no anchor nav. /privacy-policy has exactly ONE id in the whole document. scroll-behavior stays auto.
constraints.noFabrication: HARD BAN. assetRole legal.operativeText is pinned to must-not-fabricate. A generator must never write, paraphrase, summarise or 'restore' legal clauses. The schema deliberately exposes no body field for them.
constraints.signOffRequired: This is the real company's operative legal text, ported verbatim. It requires sign-off from whoever owns legal/content before any real deployment.

motion.note: No entrance or scroll animation. Global .btn hover transitions only.

responsive.desktop: single prose column; .splitter rules at 1px with 3em margin-block.
responsive.le991: column narrows with the percentage container.

notes: Two declared link repairs in the clone, both recorded rather than silently applied: a dead https://withotter.com/privacy link remapped to the local /privacy-policy route; and on /privacy-policy an orphaned href="#" wired to the one real anchor id that already existed. One in-body href="#" inside the binding-arbitration clause is deliberately LEFT INERT and flagged for content review, because synthesising an outbound URL there is a legal-content decision, not a build decision.
